Definition: from a derivative of G737; properly, something ready (or else more remotely from G142 (compare G740); something hung up), i.e. (specially) the topsail (rather foresail or jib) of a vessel:--mainsail.
BiblicalUsage: The mainsail is named once, in the shipwreck of Paul's voyage to Rome. The sailors loose the rudder bands, hoist up the mainsail to the wind, and make toward the shore, and the ship runs aground where two seas meet.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for a sail carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the picture, that men in a storm do the seaman's work and still need God to bring the ship to land.
